Hi Daniel — thanks for the spreadsheet. We can definitely provide the level of detail you requested. Summary / plan below and I attached a draft matrix and our export spec PDF for your review.

Quick summary of what I’ve included in the attached: rfi_visibility_matrix.xlsx and audit_export_specs.pdf
- Event categories: control-plane events (auth, RBAC changes), request metadata (IP, user-agent, timestamps), model inference lineage (prompt hash, model version, token counts) and redaction-able model outputs.
- Default retention: 90 days for conversational logs (opt-in longer retention available via contract), 365 days for structured audit metadata (immutable index), 7 years for legal-preservation upon signed agreement.
- Export formats: NDJSON (recommended), gzipped newline-delimited CSV for legacy tooling, and a structured tarball containing NDJSON + manifest + signed provenance bundle.
- Delivery: S3-to-S3 (customer bucket with cross-account role), presigned S3 URLs, SFTP push, and for legal holds we can coordinate secure physical media via a contracted partner. Typical exports are delivered via S3 presigned URLs.
- Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody: every export includes a manifest.json, SHA256 checksums per file, and a signed provenance token (PKI-signed timestamp assertion). For higher-assurance requests we can include notarized HSM timestamping and a signed audit ledger (Merkle-tree root + proof-of-inclusion for each record).
- SLAs: small samples (<=10k records) within 2 business days; up to 1M records usually 5–10 business days depending on retention window and redaction requests; full custody handoffs for legal-preservation require schedule negotiation (we provide a fixed project plan).

We’ve attached a KB snapshot (redwood_kb_snapshot.tar.gz) with an extract example and a sample manifest. If there are particular schemas or field-level redaction rules you need, Ben can put together a sample extractor to match your schema.

We’re happy to take the call — I suggested times on the sheet but if you prefer, Marissa can set up a technical deep-dive.

Attachments: rfi_visibility_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), audit_export_specs.pdf (application/pdf), redwood_kb_snapshot.tar.gz (application/gzip)

Sofia / Daniel — looping in some implementation detail and clarifications from infra side.

Ben and I reviewed the questions and the attached draft. Technical clarifications / specifics we recommend surfacing in the matrix:

1) Retention by event type (concrete values we will include):
   - Authentication events (login, token grants): 365 days default, WORM snapshot available on request for 7+ years.
   - API request metadata (headers, IP, URL, response code): 90 days default; can be extended to 365 days with a config flag for Dedicated and Private customers.
   - Inference lineage (prompt hash, model id, model weights tag, truncated outputs): 90 days default; full-text outputs kept 30 days by default unless customer toggles archival.

2) Export payload shape and sample sizes:
   - NDJSON schema included in audit_export_specs.pdf (we include canonical fields: event_id, timestamp_rfc3339, actor_id, org_id, event_type, resource, metadata_json, provenance_hash).
   - For large exports we generate chunked manifests (chunk size configurable; default 100k records) and provide per-chunk checksums + overall Merkle root for audit.

3) Redaction workflow:
   - Customers can request field-level or regex-based redaction prior to export. Redaction is applied server-side and documented in the manifest with redaction metadata.

4) Delivery & encryption:
   - All S3 exports are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at-rest (customer SSE-KMS optional). Presigned URLs expire after a configurable window; for long-running transfers we support multipart with resume tokens.

5) For forensic/legal handoffs we produce a signed evidence bundle: manifest.json, chain_of_custody.txt (HMAC timeline), tar.gz payload, and the PKI-signed timestamp file. We can also provide notarization via a third-party timestamping provider on request.

Example timeline we recommend putting in the RFP response: small sample (<=10k) 48–72 hours, medium (10k–100k) 3–7 days, large (>100k) negotiated but typically 1–2 weeks. For partner/private deployments timelines compress depending on access.

Ben, any additions on compression/formats?

—Marissa
